title: Document release evidence and run quality gates
description: Document tested software behavior separately from untested browser/platform combinations and unavailable physical claims, then run the complete bounded release quality-gate set for the final non-physical release.
acceptanceCriteria: Release documentation names tested software workflows, browser/platform versions, fixture scope, and dates
Untested browser/platform combinations are clearly identified rather than implied supported
Documentation disclaims physical suitability, validated tolerance, feed consistency, safe refeeding, supported-printer coverage, and physically validated calibration
Diff validation confirms no secrets, generated clutter, unrelated files, or unsupported claims
Type checking, linting, unit/contract tests, focused Playwright, accessibility, offline, recovery, and production build gates pass
Any unavailable manual or physical prerequisite is reported as a blocker rather than marked passed

steps.details: Record tested software combinations and workflows, automated/manual method, versions, fixture limits, dates, and results without broad compatibility claims.
List untested combinations and unavailable physical suitability, tolerance, consistency, refeeding, printer-support, and calibrated-profile claims in user-facing release notes.
Review changed paths for scope, secrets, artifacts, generic accessibility suppressions, external runtime dependencies, and evidence-inflating language.
Run type, lint, unit/contract, focused Playwright, automated accessibility, offline/recovery, and production build commands documented by the repository.
Summarize pass/fail results with actionable owners; keep release blocked for failed software gates or required unavailable manual checks and keep PRD 26 physically blocked.

technicalNotes: Maximum execution scope is ten minutes; run the repository's bounded release commands and focused acceptance filters.
PRD 26 remains blocked: no physical evidence exists, and release documentation must not imply otherwise.
A passing non-physical release does not validate printer behavior or a universal browser matrix.
